title: Outset Medical Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: SAN JOSE, Calif., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Outset Medical, Inc. (Nasdaq: OM), a medical technology company pioneering a first-of-its-kind technology to improve clinical outcomes in dialysis with less cost and complexity, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June
body_text: PDF Version SAN JOSE, Calif., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Outset Medical, Inc. (Nasdaq: OM), a medical technology company pioneering a first-of-its-kind technology to improve clinical outcomes in dialysis with less cost and complexity, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter and Recent Highlights Net revenue totaled $31.6 million, an increase of 1% compared to the prior-year period and an increase of 14% sequentially. Recurring revenue, consisting of Tablo consumables and services, was $22.1 million, roughly even with the prior-year period. Gross margin expanded to 42%, an increase of more than 400 basis points compared to the prior-year period. Net cash used during the quarter was $9.5 million, resulting in a total cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and restricted cash position of $151 million at quarter end. Signed a three-year, $40 million agreement with HCA Healthcare to refresh the existing fleet of Tablo systems across the nation’s largest health system. “Second quarter results reflect continued progress in strengthening the foundation of our business while positioning Outset for the next phase of growth,” said Leslie Trigg, Chair and Chief Executive Officer. “During the quarter, we completed our highest number of successful new site installations in several years. We also signed our first refresh agreement, which enhances backlog visibility and marks an important milestone as we begin to capitalize on a significant refresh opportunity. By reshaping how dialysis care is delivered across a large market that needs better solutions, Outset is well positioned to accelerate adoption, drive long-term growth and advance toward profitability.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Revenue for the second quarter was $31.6 million, an increase of 1% compared to $31.4 million in the second quarter of 2025. Product revenue of $21.9 million decreased 5% from $23.1 million in the second quarter of 2025. Service and other revenue of $9.7 million increased 17% compared to $8.3 million in the second quarter of 2025. Recurring revenue from the sale of Tablo cartridges and service was $22.1 million, compared to $22.5 million in the prior-year period. Gross profit of $13.3 million increased 12% from $11.9 million in the second quarter of 2025. Gross margin was 42.0%, compared to 37.8% in the second quarter of 2025. On a non-GAAP basis, gross margin reached 42.2%, as compared to 38.4% in the second quarter of 2025. Product gross profit was $10.1 million, compared to $11.3 million in the second quarter of 2025. Product gross margin was 46.1%, compared to 48.9% in the second quarter of 2025. Service and other gross profit was $3.2 million, compared to $0.6 million in the second quarter of 2025. Service and other gross margin was 32.6%, compared to 6.9% in the second quarter of 2025. Operating expenses of $29.0 million were roughly even with the prior-year period. Research and development (R&D) expenses were $5.5 million, sales and marketing (S&M) expenses were $12.2 million, and general and administrative (G&A) expenses were $11.4 million. This compared to operating expenses of $28.7 million in the second quarter of 2025, including R&D expenses of $5.3 million, S&M expenses of $14.3 million, and G&A expenses of $9.2 million. Excluding stock-based compensation expense and litigation charges, non-GAAP operating expenses were $25.8 million, including R&D expenses of $4.9 million, S&M expenses of $11.7 million, and G&A expenses of $9.2 million. Net loss was $18.0 million compared to net loss of $18.5 million for the same period in 2025. On a non-GAAP basis, net loss was $14.7 million, which is relatively consistent with the same period in 2025. Total cash, including restricted cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, was $151.0 million as of June 30, 2026. 2026 Financial Guidance Outset reiterated its 2026 revenue guidance of $125 million to $130 million, a 5% to 9% increase over $119.5 million in 2025. The Company continues to expect non-GAAP gross margin to range between the low-40% to mid-40% range for the full year. Conference Call Details Outset will host a conference call today, August 6, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. PT / 4:30 p.m. ET to discuss second quarter results. Those interested in accessing the live or archived version of the conference call can visit the “Investors” section of the Outset Medical website at https://investors.outsetmedical.com . Those interested in participating in the call via telephone may register online here . Once registered, participants will receive a dial-in number and unique PIN to join the call. Participants are encouraged to register more than 15 minutes before the start of the call. Cinder raises $41 million in Series B funding to defend companies from AI abuse
summary: Companies spend tens of billions of dollars a year on solutions that can't even keep their biggest safety problems out of sight.
body_text: NEW YORK, NY — New York, NY - Cinder, mission-critical infrastructure protecting the world's most innovative companies from digital abuse and manipulation, today announced its series B funding round of $41 million, led by Radical Ventures, with participation from Accel, Y Combinator, M12, Microsoft's Venture Fund, PSP Growth, and Neuberger’s Outpost Ventures, among others. Cinder also announced the opening of its corporate headquarters in New York City. The company plans to double headcount in the next 12 months. "Trust and safety has gone from a back-office function to critical infrastructure that directly affects enterprise value and brand integrity. As AI-generated content explodes — and as AI agents increasingly act on companies' behalf — traditional moderation tools simply don't work. Cinder is the only AI-native platform built for this shift, and it's already become mission-critical for the world's most innovative AI companies as they scale safely and responsibly,” said Ryan Shannon, Partner at Radical Ventures. Top technology platforms, including OpenAI, Spotify, depop, and Black Forest Labs, use Cinder to navigate the most pressing and cutting edge online safety challenges in the world, and defuse threats that could harm their users, brand, and business. Trained on a company's values and policies, Cinder’s AI agents detect, adapt, and respond to digital threats in real time, like fraud, AI prompt abuse, and non-consensual intimate imagery. Cinder's platform then automates enforcement across every guideline a company sets – so AI models behave as intended, content moderation works at scale, and regulatory obligations are met. “When the world's most innovative AI labs and consumer platforms all rely on the same team to defend their users, that's a category leader. Cinder is becoming as essential to modern platforms as identity or payments, and in the AI era this is arguably the most critical infrastructure layer,” said Sara Ittelson, Partner at Accel. "Few issues are as important for platforms as managing their trust and safety," said Peter Lenke, Managing Partner at M12, Microsoft's Venture Fund. "As AI accelerates the reach, frequency and efficacy of bad actors, it has never been more important for companies to leverage technology to protect their users. Cinder provides the most innovative companies in the market a unified operating system for their safety operations while preserving each company's unique values, policies, and brand voice. The result is enforcement that actually works at scale, freeing human moderators to focus on the most complex cases and making the internet and their customers’ products safer for everyone." Cinder's founding team has been on the front lines fighting the internet's worst crimes, including nation-state espionage, terrorist coordination, and child sexual abuse rings. Cinder CEO Glen Wise is a former CIA cyber analyst and security engineer on Facebook's Threat Discovery team. He founded Cinder to make sure the people defending the internet had the same firepower as the people attacking it. “The internet has always been abused by bad actors, and AI is making this exponentially worse,” Wise said. “Unchecked abuse on the internet destroys trust, and without trust, you don't have a business. The sheer volume and diversity of threats have made it nearly impossible for any team to keep up, no matter how talented or well-resourced they are. Cinder is the bouncer of the internet. We’re here to help you throw the bad guys out.” AI has fundamentally changed the digital threat landscape. Bad actors now have access to more powerful tools than the platforms they're targeting, creating abuse, fraud, and manipulation at unprecedented scale and speed. Defending the internet isn't a support function but is one of the most important responsibilities in technology today. Cinder treats it that way. ABOUT CINDER: Founded in 2022, Cinder is the mission-critical infrastructure protecting the world's most innovative platforms from digital abuse, fraud, and manipulation. Cinder's tools detect threats in real time, and deploy agents to automate content review and policy enforcement. Trusted by OpenAI, Spotify, depop, and Black Forest Labs, Cinder gives trust and safety teams the firepower to stay ahead of the overwhelming volume and velocity of threats in the AI era. ### About Cinder Founded in 2022, Cinder is the mission-critical infrastructure protecting the world's most innovative platforms from digital abuse, fraud, and manipulation. body_text: View All News HALOZYME REPORTS RECORD SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS, BEATS ESTIMATES AND RAISES FULL YEAR 2026 FINANCIAL GUIDANCE August 6, 2026 Total Revenue Increased 48% YOY to $481 million Royalty Revenue Increased 50% YOY to $308 million Raises 2026 Financial Guidance Ranges: Total Revenue of $1.835 - $1.910 billion, YOY Growth of 31% - 37% Royalty Revenue of $1.220 - $1.245 billion, YOY Growth of 41% - 43% Adjusted EBITDA of $1.225 - $1.280 billion, YOY Growth of 86% - 95% 1 Non-GAAP Diluted EPS of $8.65 - $9.00, YOY Growth of 108% - 117% 1 Signed Five New ENHANZE ® and Hypercon ™ Collaboration Agreements YTD 2026, Exceeding Goal of Three for Full Year 2026 SAN DIEGO , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HALO) ("Halozyme" or the "Company") today reported its financial and operating results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided an update on its recent corporate activities. "We delivered another quarter of strong performance, with multiple proof points demonstrating the attractive features of ENHANZE as a compounding platform engine: repeatability of success, scalability, diversification and durability of revenues," said Dr. Helen Torley, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Total revenue increased 48% year-over-year to $481 million, royalty revenue increased 50% to $308 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 46% to $329 million, reflecting the strength of our differentiated royalty business. Based on these record results, we are raising our full year 2026 financial guidance." "Importantly, we are delivering on both our near-term and long-term growth objectives. The ENHANZE value proposition is attracting new partners and additional products from our current partners. We expanded our royalty revenue opportunity by signing five new ENHANZE and Hypercon collaborations through July, including agreements with Vertex, Oruka, GSK, Incyte and an undisclosed partner who is the first to license ENHANZE for a nucleic acid therapeutic. We have also demonstrated our commitment to returning significant capital to shareholders, repurchasing $333 million of shares in 2Q 2026, at an average price of $69.30. Overall, these results illustrate our continued ability to create multiple waves of revenue opportunities that will drive long-term shareholder value," concluded Dr. Torley. Second Quarter Corporate Highlight: In May 2026, the Company announced a new share repurchase program to repurchase up to $1.0 billion of its outstanding common stock by December 31, 2028, with an expectation of buying back at least $400 million of shares in 2026. During the second quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased 4.8 million shares for $332.8 million at an average price of $69.30 per share under the May 2026 and February 2024 share repurchase programs. The February 2024 share repurchase program was completed in June 2026. Recent Partner Highlights: In July 2026, Halozyme and Incyte entered into a global collaboration and license agreement to evaluate additional subcutaneous formulations of INCA033989, a first-in-class mutant calreticulin ("mutCALR")-targeted monoclonal antibody, in patients with mutCALR-expressing myeloproliferative neoplasms ("MPNs"), utilizing Halozyme's proprietary ENHANZE® drug delivery technology. Under the collaboration, Incyte also has the option to nominate up to two additional targets for use with ENHANZE®. Under the terms of the agreement, Incyte agreed to make an upfront payment and potential future milestone payments and royalties on net sales of products developed with ENHANZE®. In the third quarter of 2026, the ongoing ARGX-119 adimanebart program was expanded to include a Phase 1 SC bioavailability study with ENHANZE®. Second Quarter Partner Highlights: In May 2026, Halozyme and an undisclosed company entered into a global collaboration and license agreement that provides the company access to ENHANZE® to develop a nucleic acid therapeutic. In May 2026, Janssen announced pivotal results from the Phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 study showing that subcutaneous amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj delivered durable responses in patients with advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma previously treated with immunotherapy and chemotherapy and submitted a supplemental Biologics License Application ("sBLA") to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA"). In May 2026, Viatris initiated a Phase 1 study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of a single dose of selatogrel in Chinese adults with chronic coronary syndrome. In May 2026, argenx announced FDA approval of a sBLA for VYVGART® Hytrulo with ENHANZE® for the treatment of adult patients with generalized myasthenia gravis including all serotypes – anti-AChR-Ab positive, anti-MuSK-Ab positive, anti-LRP4-Ab positive, and triple seronegative. In May 2026, Halozyme and GSK plc ("GSK") entered into a global collaboration and license agreement for ENHANZE® with multiple oncology targets, including the first potential application in antibody-drug conjugates. Under the terms of the agreement, GSK made an upfront payment and agreed to make potential future milestone payments and royalties on net sales of products developed with ENHANZE®. In May 2026, Halozyme and Oruka Therapeutics, Inc. ("Oruka") entered into a global exclusive collaboration and license agreement for Halozyme's Hypercon™ technology for use with ORKA-001, in development for psoriasis and related inflammatory diseases and one additional target. Under the terms of the agreement, Oruka made an upfront payment and agreed to make potential future milestone payments and mid-single digit royalties on net sales of products developed using the Hypercon™ technology. In May 2026, Takeda announced positive topline results from its pivotal Phase 2/3 trial of TAK-881 with ENHANZE® in Primary Immunodeficiency Disease. In April 2026, Halozyme and Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated ("Vertex") entered into a global exclusive collaboration and license agreement that provides Vertex access to Halozyme's Hypercon™ technology for use in up to three targets. Under the terms of the agreement, Vertex made a $15 million upfront payment and agreed to make potential future milestone payments and royalties on net sales of products developed using the Hypercon™ technology. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights: Total revenue was $481.0 million, compared to $325.7 million in the second quarter of 2025. The 48% year-over-year increase was primarily driven by royalty revenue growth and an increase in product sales. Revenue included $307.7 million in royalties, an increase of 50% compared to $205.6 million in the second quarter of 2025, primarily driven by continued sales uptake of ENHANZE® partner products that have launched since 2020, predominantly by VYVGART® Hytrulo by argenx and DARZALEX® SC Janssen in all geographies and contributions from other recently launched products. Cost of sales was $79.2 million, compared to $46.4 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of sales was primarily due to an increase in bulk rHuPH20 sales. Amortization of intangibles expense was $29.5 million, compared to $17.8 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase in amortization of intangibles expense was due to the acquisition of Elektrofi, Inc. ("Elektrofi") in November 2025. Research and development expense was $27.7 million, compared to $17.5 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the acquisition of Elektrofi and Surf Bio, Inc. ("Surf Bio") in the fourth quarter of 2025. Selling, general and administrative expense was $57.0 million, compared to $41.6 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in consulting and professional service fees, including litigation costs incurred in connection with patent infringement litigation, the acquisition of Elektrofi and Surf Bio, and an increase in compensation expense. Operating income was $287.7 million, compared to $202.4 million in the second quarter of 2025. Net income was $229.9 million, compared to $165.2 million in the second quarter of 2025. EBITDA was $321.9 million, compared to $222.9 million in the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $328.8 million, compared to $225.5 million in the second quarter of 2025.1 GAAP diluted earnings per share was $1.90, compared to $1.33 in the second quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was $2.28, compared to $1.54 in the second quarter of 2025.1 Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities were $231.9 million on June 30, 2026, compared to $145.4 million on December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by cash generated from operations. Financial Outlook for 2026 The Company is raising its 2026 financial guidance ranges, which were last provided on May 11, 2026. For the full year 2026, the Company expects: Total revenue of $1.835 billion to $1.910 billion, representing growth of 31% to 37% over 2025 total revenue, primarily driven by increases in royalty revenue and product sales from API. Revenue from royalties of $1.220 billion to $1.245 billion, representing growth of 41% to 43% over 2025. Adjusted EBITDA of $1.225 billion to $1.280 billion, representing growth of 86% to 95% over 2025, including new Hypercon™ and Surf Bio investments of approximately $60 million. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $8.65 to $9.00, representing growth of 108% to 117% over 2025. The Company's earnings per share guidance includes new Hypercon™ and Surf Bio investments of approximately $60 million and does not consider the impact of potential future share repurchases. About Halozyme Halozyme is a biopharmaceutical company advancing disruptive solutions to improve patient experiences and outcomes for emerging and established therapies. As the innovators of ENHANZE® drug delivery technology with the proprietary enzyme rHuPH20, Halozyme's commercially-validated solution facilitates the subcutaneous delivery of injected drugs and fluids, reducing treatment burden and improving convenience. ENHANZE® has touched more than one million patient lives through ten commercialized products across over 100 global markets and is licensed to leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies including Roche, Takeda, Pfizer, Janssen, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, Bristol-Myers Squibb, argenx, ViiV Healthcare, Chugai Pharmaceutical, Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Merus N.V., Skye Bioscience, GSK and Incyte. Halozyme expanded its drug delivery technology portfolio to develop partner products using Hypercon™ and Surf Bio's hyperconcentration technology. Hypercon™ is an innovative microparticle technology expected to set a new standard in hyperconcentration of drugs and biologics by reducing injection volume for the same dosage and enabling administration in at-home and healthcare-provider settings. The addition of Surf Bio's polymer-based hyperconcentration technology further broadens the range of biologics that can be delivered subcutaneously, meaningfully expanding the scope of opportunities across therapeutic modalities. Together, Hypercon™ and Surf Bio's technology complement ENHANZE® by enabling creation and delivery of highly concentrated biologics. The Hypercon™ technology has been licensed to leading biopharmaceutical partners, including Janssen, Eli Lilly, argenx, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, and Oruka Therapeutics. Halozyme also develops, manufactures and commercializes drug-device combination products using advanced auto-injector technologies designed to improve convenience, reliability and tolerability, enhancing patient comfort and adherence. The Company has two proprietary commercial products, Hylenex® and XYOSTED®, partnered commercial products and ongoing development programs with Teva Pharmaceuticals and McDermott Laboratories Limited, an affiliate of Viatris Inc. Halozyme is headquartered in San Diego, CA, with offices in Ewing, NJ; Minnetonka, MN; and Boston, MA. Minnetonka is also the site of its operations facility. For more information, visit www.halozyme.com and connect with us on LinkedIn. Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to disclosing financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"), this press release and the accompanying tables contain certain Non-GAAP financial measures. The Company reports earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ("EBITDA"), adjusted EBITDA, Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share, Non-GAAP diluted shares, and guidance with respect to those measures, in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. The Company calculates Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share excluding share-based compensation expense, amortization of debt discounts, intangible asset amortization, one-time items, if any, such as changes in contingent liabilities, inventory adjustments, impairment charges, transaction costs for business combinations and share-based compensation acceleration expenses, intellectual property litigation costs, inducement expenses related to convertible notes, and certain adjustments to income tax expense. The Company calculates Non-GAAP diluted shares excluding the dilutive impact of convertible notes which is used in calculating Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share. The Company calculates EBITDA excluding interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. The Company calculates adjusted EBITDA excluding one-time items, if any, such as changes in contingent liabilities, inventory adjustments, impairment charges, transaction costs for business combinations and share-based compensation acceleration expenses and intellectual property litigation costs. Reconciliations between GAAP and Non-GAAP financial measures are included at the end of this press release. The Company provides Non-GAAP financial measures that it believes will be achieved; however, it cannot accurately predict all of the components of the adjusted calculations and the GAAP measures may be materially different than the Non-GAAP measures. The Company evaluates other items of income and expense on an individual basis for potential inclusion in the calculation of Non-GAAP financial measures and considers both the quantitative and qualitative aspects of the item, including (i) its size and nature, (ii) whether or not it relates to the Company's ongoing business operations and (iii) whether or not the Company expects it to occur as part of the Company's normal business on a regular basis. title: Woodward Dream Cruise: Celebrating What We Do in Detroit
summary: Much has been written about Metro Detroit’s Dream Cruise, and a lot of it misses the forest for the trees. The oft-repeated origin story is heartwarming and true: a 1990s cruise on Woodward Avenue that started as a charity event meant to raise money for a soccer field. That cruise mimicked the auto enthusiast scene […]
body_text: Much has been written about Metro Detroit’s Dream Cruise, and a lot of it misses the forest for the trees. The oft-repeated origin story is heartwarming and true: a 1990s cruise on Woodward Avenue that started as a charity event meant to raise money for a soccer field. That cruise mimicked the auto enthusiast scene on an Oakland County stretch of Woodward in the ‘50s, ’60s, and early ‘70s. The event’s popularity snowballed, and soon began attracting tens of thousands of hot rods and classics and nearly a million spectators. That feel-good coverage from outside the car world is now occasionally accompanied by complaints about the noise, the blocked streets, the inconvenience of it all. And, because most observers arrive in mid-afternoon, they are dismayed to see the predominance of SUVs and other ordinary stuff in the cruising lanes, each packed with gawkers who want to be part of the action and are content to admire the classics and rods, by then parked at the sides of the avenue, from afar. That’s not the Dream Cruise. At least it’s not my version. My cruise is a giant week-long celebration of what we do in Metro Detroit. We celebrate the fact that we make cars and trucks, and lots of them. We design them, engineer them, assemble them, advertise them, repair them, and even write about them. If we don’t touch those Motown products directly, we might bake bread for the people who build them, teach their children, or care for them when they’re not well. Here in “the D,” we are all about cars. And every year for a week we celebrate that with a big party we call the Dream Cruise. Mike Schenden climbs into his pretty black Stingray Paul Stenquist Brad Mali entertains the troops on his Buell Cyclone. Paul Stenquist Most of the gang assembled in Steve Guenther’s backyard in celebration of cruise week and what we do here in “the D.” Paul Stenquist This doesn’t just take place on the street. It’s in backyards and bars on the banks of mighty Woodward and all over town. It’s anywhere car people gather to reminisce, show off their hardware, and tell lies. I show up at one of these parties every year. It’s an invitation-only event held in the backyard of a former Budweiser distributor named Steve Guenther . Steve, who once kept Detroiters in suds is now the pied piper of Detroit car folk. He knows everyone in the biz and can tell you what each of them drives. That’s our gracious host Steve Guenther pointing. The car is Don Cenker’s ’40 Ford. Paul Stenquist The well-fashioned interior of Cenker’s ’40 Ford. Paul Stenquist I thought it would be nice this year to take Hagerty readers along to Steve’s annual cruise celebration. Any car guy or gal would enjoy the folks who gather at Steve’s place on Wednesday of cruise week. Some of the attendees made their living creating cars and earned a place in automotive history. Many are former or current GM, Ford, and Stellantis employees. Others just have a passion for great rolling stock and live it. Among them this year was Jerry Harkey, who was a powerplant engineer at Chrysler and helped develop the Gen III Hemi. Jerry arrived in his ‘55 Packard Patrician, a car he’s owned for more than half a century. Also joining the festivities were Tom and Carolyn Peters. Tom spearheaded Corvette design development for many years and is an automotive icon. Carolyn is a designer as well who created many automotive interiors and now heads her own design firm. Tom arrived in his 396-powered red-on-red ’65 Impala convertible. Carolyn rumbled in at the wheel of her extensively reworked 440 six-pack ’69 Dodge Super Bee. Then there were GM crate-engine guru Brad Nye in a hot Camaro, Peterbilt dealership owners Greg and Amy Reefer in their totally streetable 8-second, 140-mph 2003 Mustang Mach 1, and Steve’s neighbor (and brother from another mother) Brad Mali burning the tire off the rim of his Buell M2 Cyclone naked motorcycle. (Brad was fully dressed. Only the motorcycle was naked.) Brad Mali, Carolyn Peters, and Brad’s son check out Carolyn’s massively powerful, heavily modified 6-pack Dodge Super Bee. Paul Stenquist Jerry Harkey, a former Chrysler powerplant engineer, owns this Packard Patrician and numerous other interesting classics. Paul Stenquist Tom Peters’ gorgeous ’65 Super Sport convertible. Paul Stenquist Tom Peters arrived in his red-on-red ’65 Super Sport. The big block car is a real manual-shift, air-conditioned convertible. Paul Stenquist The gathering begins on Steve’s long driveway and on the street in front of his house where folks move from car to car, admiring the hardware, and talking shop. Eventually, the group moves to the backyard for Coneys dressed in Steve’s own potent chili and assorted snacks. Passengers down some Buds, of course. After some more spirited conversation, the cars fire up, and all head east to Woodward for an hour or so of cruising. At 9 p.m. sharp, they pull into the parking lot of a shuttered restaurant. Steve, who can talk almost anyone into almost anything, has convinced the establishment to reopen for the gang and serve them a late meal. The laughter rings out until the night finally ends with a toast to Motor City and what we do here. We make cars. Rusty Bucket, a local restaurant, served us after hours. There we toasted the Motor City and reaffirmed what we do here. We make cars! Paul Stenquist The gang gathers in Steve’s backyard prior to cruising Woodward. Wednesday is the best day to cruise. More real classics; fewer gawkers in SUVs. Paul Stenquist A waitress from the restaurant where the evening will end takes the order of Amy Reefer. Amy, with her husband Greg, sells Peterbilt trucks. Paul Stenquist The post Woodward Dream Cruise: Celebrating What We Do in Detroit appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Telenor selects Vodafone to manage its international voice operations across Nordic markets and Maritime
summary: Telenor and Vodafone Procure & Connect today announced an agreement for Vodafone to manage Telenor’s international voice operations, currently operated by Telenor Linx, across Telenor Norway, Telenor Sweden, DNA Finland, Telenor Denmark and Telenor Maritime.
body_text: Oslo / Luxembourg – 13 August 2026 : Telenor and Vodafone Procure & Connect today announced an agreement for Vodafone to manage Telenor’s international voice operations, currently operated by Telenor Linx, across Telenor Norway, Telenor Sweden, DNA Finland, Telenor Denmark and Telenor Maritime. The agreement enables Telenor to leverage Vodafone’s global scale, international voice expertise and established operating platform. As international communications continue to evolve, operators increasingly require trusted partners to manage global voice services securely, reliably and at scale. Under the arrangement, Vodafone Procure & Connect will act as the operational gateway for inbound and outbound international voice traffic into and out of Telenor’s Nordic markets and Telenor Maritime. The agreement is designed to support the future operation of Telenor’s international voice business while maintaining the high standards expected by customers and partners. The transition will be delivered through a phased migration programme over the coming six months. Telenor Linx’s existing customer and partner agreements will continue to be honoured throughout the transition period, ensuring a structured and orderly migration process. This arrangement does not affect customer services, existing commercial relationships or agreed voice interconnect services. Stig Waagbo, CEO Telenor Linx, said: “As the telecommunications industry continues to evolve, strategic partnerships play a crucial role in driving efficiency and delivering greater value to customers. This agreement with Vodafone reflects our commitment to optimizing our operations while maintaining the highest standards of service. We are confident that Vodafone is the right partner to support this next chapter of our voice business.” Kenneth Graham, Managing Director of Voice & Roaming Services, said: “Managing international voice services at scale requires deep expertise, trusted relationships and robust security capabilities. Telenor's decision to select Vodafone reflects the strength of our platform and the capabilities we have built. We welcome the opportunity to support Telenor’s customers and further strengthen the partnership between our companies.” -ends- About Telenor Linx Telenor Linx is an international carrier and software company delivering services to the global telco industry. Telenor Linx operates at the intersection of international telecommunications and digital services. The company partners with mobile network operators and global digital players such as Google, Meta, and Netflix to enable seamless, secure digital connectivity and monetization worldwide. Through its global platform, Telenor Linx connects the telco and digital ecosystems, helping partners expand reach and deliver enhanced digital experiences. Telenor Linx is part of the Telenor Group. For more information, visit www.telenorlinx.com About Telenor Telenor Group is a leading telecommunications and technology company in the Nordics and Asia, serving over 200 million customers and generating annual revenues of around NOK 80 billion (2024). Telenor holds strong positions in its markets and is committed to responsible business conduct. Driven by Telenor’s purpose, “With you, for a safer and smarter tomorrow”, we aim to create impact beyond connectivity by enabling societies to thrive in a digital future. Our cultural foundation is built on Trust, Curiosity, and Passion, guiding how we collaborate, innovate and deliver value for customers and communities. Connectivity has been Telenor’s domain for more than 165 years, and today we combine that heritage with forward-looking solutions for security, sustainability and inclusion. Telenor is listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange under the ticker TEL. For more information, visit https://www.telenor.com. About Vodafone Procure & Connect Vodafone Procure & Connect is the telecommunications industry’s benchmark for procurement excellence combined with one of the world’s most trusted global voice and roaming capabilities. We help businesses simplify procurement and deliver seamless connectivity, enabling smarter operations and stronger performance in a fast-changing digital world. Our mission is to lead the future of procurement and global connectivity, leveraging scale, expertise and innovation to deliver exceptional value for our customers, partners and stakeholders. For more information, please visit vodafone.com/procureandconnect or connect with us on LinkedIn . About Vodafone Group everyone.connected Vodafone is a leading European and African telecoms company. We serve over 340 million mobile and broadband customers, operating networks in 15 countries with investments in a further five and partners in over 40 more. Our undersea cables transport around a sixth of the world’s internet traffic, and we are developing a new direct-to-mobile satellite communications service to connect areas without coverage. Vodafone runs one of the world’s largest IoT platforms, with 205 million IoT connections globally, and we provide financial services to around 88 million customers across seven African countries – managing more transactions than any other provider. From the seabed to the stars, Vodafone’s purpose is to keep everyone connected. For more information, please visit www.vodafone.com follow us on X at @VodafoneGroup or connect with us on LinkedIn at www.linkedin.com/company/vodafone.

title: Understanding Types and Definition of Asset in Business Accounting
summary: An asset in accounting is a resource owned by a business expecting future benefits, including current and non-current, tangible, and intangible types.
body_text: Assets are the backbone of any business’s financial strength, supporting growth, resilience, and long-term success. Effective asset management has become essential for companies striving to optimise operations and secure financial stability, particularly as the UAE’s economy expands across booming sectors like finance, construction, and manufacturing. Companies are now turning to digital tools and smarter financial practices to keep track of assets, manage expenditures, and streamline operations. According to a report by Grand View Research, the global asset management market was valued at approximately USD 458.02 billion in 2023 and is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 36.4% from 2024 to 2030. This significant growth underscores the increasing importance of strategic asset management in enhancing operational efficiency and financial performance across various industries. With real-time insights into assets and expenses, businesses can make informed decisions, prevent overspending, and improve productivity—ultimately creating a stronger foundation for long-term growth. What Exactly Is an Asset? In accounting, assets are defined as resources owned or controlled by a business that are expected to provide future economic benefits. They form the foundation of your business’s financial health and include everything from cash and inventory to machinery and patents. By assessing your assets, you can determine your organisation’s net worth, solvency, and profitability. Understanding the various types of assets is essential for evaluating your business’s financial position. See the finance-side view of assets as resources that create future value , which frames the same concept slightly differently. The Various Types of Assets Explained Assets are classified into different categories, and knowing these distinctions is crucial for a comprehensive assessment of a business’s financial status. [cta-10] 1. Current Assets Current assets refer to resources that can be easily converted into cash , improving liquidity and supporting operational stability. These assets are fundamental for day-to-day expenses and can be accessed readily. Common examples include: Cash : Funds readily available for immediate use. Accounts Receivable : Money owed by customers for goods or services sold on credit, critical for cash flow. Inventory : Goods available for sale or materials for production, essential for meeting customer demand without overstocking. Efficient management of current assets ensures you can meet short-term obligations without financial strain, maintaining both liquidity and operational efficiency. 2. Fixed or Non-Current Assets Fixed assets, also known as long-term assets, are resources intended for long-term use and not easily converted into cash. These are crucial for daily operations and future growth. Examples include: Buildings : Properties used for business operations or rental purposes. Machinery : Equipment used in manufacturing or service delivery. Vehicles : Company-owned cars or trucks for operational use. Fixed assets are vital to a business but depreciate over time, impacting financial statements and tax deductions. 3. Tangible Assets Tangible assets are physical items that play a significant role in production and revenue generation, especially in industries like manufacturing and retail. Examples include: Property, Plant, and Equipment (PP&E) : Assets essential for production, logistics, and operations. Vehicles : Used for transporting goods or providing services. Effective management of tangible assets is key to maintaining financial health and meeting operational demands. 4. Intangible Assets Intangible assets are non-physical resources that add value to a business, such as intellectual property and brand recognition. These are particularly important in sectors like pharmaceuticals and technology. Examples include: Patents : Legal rights for inventions that provide competitive advantages. Trademarks : Distinctive signs or logos that enhance brand recognition and consumer trust. Goodwill : The value from reputation, customer loyalty, and other factors that can drive profitability. Intangible assets, though challenging to measure, contribute significantly to long-term profitability and competitive edge. 5. Operating Assets Operating assets are directly related to core business activities essential for revenue generation and productivity. Examples include: Machinery : Used in manufacturing or service delivery to meet demand. Property : Real estate used for business operations, such as offices or warehouses. Vehicles : Company-owned vehicles for transporting goods or providing customer service. Managing operating assets effectively supports customer demands and offers tax benefits through depreciation. 6. Non-Operating Assets Non-operating assets generate revenue but aren’t essential for daily operations. They provide passive income and add financial stability. Examples include: Investment Properties: Real estate holdings generating rental income. Marketable Securities: Investments that can be quickly liquidated. These assets provide financial flexibility and stability, often serving as collateral or supporting cash flow during constraints. See where these categories actually sit within a full balance sheet , alongside liabilities and equity. Why Assets Matter in Business Accounting Assets play a significant role in business operations, including: Financial Stability : Assets help meet day-to-day obligations and pay off short-term liabilities, maintaining smooth cash flow. Long-term Stability : They provide the necessary infrastructure for growth and expansion and can be leveraged for liquidity during times of need. Risk Management : Assets support solvency and can be used as collateral when obtaining long-term financing. Reviewing and optimising asset classification must align with business needs and strategic planning. See the liabilities side of the same balance sheet equation for the full picture of what a business owns versus owes. The Critical Role of Assets in Financial Management Strategic asset management is vital for your organisation’s financial development. It aligns asset investments with business goals, ensuring returns on investments and strengthening the risk management framework. Effective asset management influences cash flow, provides tax benefits, and enhances reporting accuracy, ultimately improving financial planning. How Alaan Can Support Financial Management At Alaan, we simplify expense management, empowering businesses with real-time financial insights and precise control over their spending. Our platform is designed to help you track expenses accurately and maintain financial clarity, supporting smarter budgeting and resource allocation. With Alaan, your business gains: Real-Time Expense Tracking : Monitor every expense, from operational costs to asset-related spending, instantly. Our platform provides visibility into where funds are allocated, preventing overspending and supporting budget adherence. AI-Powered Expense Categorisation : Our intelligent automation categorises expenses accurately, ensuring every cost is aligned with the right category. This reduces manual errors and keeps asset-related expenses organized for easy access and reporting. VAT Compliance Automation : We’ve built VAT compliance checks directly into our platform. Alaan automatically verifies receipts, extracting essential VAT details such as Tax Registration Number (TRN) and VAT amounts. This helps ensure compliance for tax-deductible expenses, adding financial security and ease during tax season. Integration with Leading Accounting Software : Alaan seamlessly syncs with popular accounting software like Xero and QuickBooks, ensuring your records are always up-to-date. This integration streamlines month-end reconciliations and simplifies asset-related reporting, saving you time and reducing administrative workload. Actionable Financial Insights : Alaan provides data-driven insights into spending trends and asset utilisation. Our reports help identify areas for cost savings and optimisation, supporting your strategic planning and helping you make informed financial decisions. Alaan’s tools enhance your financial control, helping your business allocate resources wisely, manage expenses efficiently, and build a resilient financial foundation. [cta-9] Conclusion Grasping the nuances of asset management extends beyond basic accounting ; it is essential for the success of your business. Effectively classifying and strategically managing assets can significantly enhance your organisation’s financial wellbeing by assessing its risk exposure and profitability. By taking a proactive approach to asset management, you can identify opportunities for optimisation, ensure compliance with financial regulations, and make informed decisions that drive growth. At Alaan , we’re here to support smarter financial management. Our tools offer real-time insights and seamless integrations that help keep your financial planning on track. title: Repair Procedures Belong at Every Step
summary: Learn how integrating OEM repair procedures throughout the repair process helps collision repair shops improve accuracy, documentation, and customer trust.
body_text: Ask any collision repairer what has changed most over the past decade, and you’ll probably hear some version of the same answer: the cars got smarter, and the repairs got more complicated. That is why repair procedures can’t be treated like something you look up once, print, and tuck away. They need to be available at every step of the repair—from the first estimate to the final customer conversation. When your team can see the right procedure at the right moment, you reduce guessing. There is a stronger repair plan. Technicians get clearer direction. And there’s better documentation about why certain operations, parts, scans, calibrations, or inspections are needed. And you can give customers a better explanation than, “That’s what the estimate says.” Start With The Estimate, But Don’t Stop There A good repair starts before the vehicle hits production. Having repair procedures available while writing or reviewing the estimate helps the team catch required operations early instead of finding them halfway through the job. This is especially useful when procedures are accessible through the tools your team already uses. For example, CCC’s Repair Methods can be accessed on a desktop, on the web, or even from a technician’s phone in the CCC ONE® Mobile App. That way, it’s easy to confirm requirements while reviewing damage, building a supplement, or answering a question from the floor. The goal is not to turn every estimator into a walking repair manual. The goal is to make procedure checks a normal part of the workflow. Bring The Procedure To The Bay Even the best estimate can lose value if the information does not make it to the technician doing the work. Many decisions are made at the car. Is there a one-time-use part? Does the OEM call for a specific weld location, sectioning point, corrosion protection step, scan, or calibration? Does a panel replacement require removing another component first? These are not details you want to leave to memory. Procedures need to be easy to pull up at the vehicle, in the stall, and during teardown—not just saved somewhere in the job file. Because when technicians can pull up repair methods in the bay, the procedure becomes part of the repair—not paperwork after the fact. This ensures a safe, complete repair for the customer. Use Procedures To Explain The Repair Repair procedures also help outside the production area. They can make customer conversations clearer and less stressful. Most customers do not understand why a “small hit” can lead to a bigger repair plan. They see a bumper cover. You see sensors, brackets, calibrations, materials, safety systems, and manufacturer requirements. Showing or referencing the repair procedure helps connect the dots. Instead of saying, “We have to do this,” your team can say, “Here’s what the manufacturer requires for this repair, and here’s why it affects safety, timing, and cost.” That kind of explanation builds trust. It also helps customers understand that the shop is not adding work for the sake of adding work. The shop is following the information needed to repair the vehicle properly. Make It A Shop Habit The shops that get the most value from repair procedures do not treat them as a last-minute check. They build them into the process. Check procedures during estimating and repair planning. Make sure technicians can access them at the vehicle. Document the procedures used on the job. Use procedure information to explain repairs to customers and insurers. Review misses or supplements and ask, “Would earlier access to the procedure have changed this?” That is the real impact. Repair procedures help shops move from “we’ve always done it this way” to “we know this is the right way for this vehicle.” For a busy shop, that can mean fewer surprises, better documentation, stronger customer conversations, and more confidence across the team. See how CCC Repair Methods can help bring OEM repair procedures into more of your repair process.

title: Reading level chart by grade: Lexile, F&P, DRA, and grade equivalents in one place
summary: One chart that cross-references Lexile, Fountas and Pinnell, DRA, and grade equivalents from kindergarten through high school, plus what each system measures and how to use them at home.
body_text: How to figure out your kid's reading level at home If your child attends a school that uses F&P or DRA, you likely already have a level from their last assessment. If you homeschool or want an independent check, here are practical options: Lexile: many standardized tests (MAP, STAR, state assessments) report a Lexile score. You can also use the free Lexile tool at lexile.com to find books at your child's level Informal running record: pick a book you think is close to your kid's level. Have them read a page aloud. If they miss more than 1 in 10 words, it's too hard for independent reading. If they read every word effortlessly, it's too easy for growth. The right level is where they stumble occasionally but can still follow the story Interest-led assessment: sometimes the best "level" is whatever book your kid won't put down. A child reading below grade level who devours Dog Man is building fluency faster than a child reading at grade level who avoids books entirely For a more structured at-home approach, our back-to-school reading assessment guide walks through how to check your kid's level before the school year starts. What to do when the numbers don't match It's common for a child to test at one level in Lexile and a different level in F&P. A few reasons this happens: The systems measure different things. Lexile is algorithmic (word frequency and sentence length). F&P is observational (accuracy, fluency, comprehension, self-correction). A child who decodes well but struggles with comprehension may score higher on Lexile than F&P Assessment conditions vary. A formal F&P running record administered by a trained teacher in a quiet room will produce different results than a Lexile score derived from a 30-minute computer-adaptive test taken in a noisy classroom Growth isn't linear. Kids develop reading skills in bursts. A child might jump two F&P levels over a summer of enthusiastic reading and then plateau for months. Both patterns are normal When numbers conflict, trust the system that captures the most information about your specific child. For most homeschool families, that means a combination of the informal running record (which you can do yourself) and your daily observation of what your kid reads independently, how they handle unfamiliar words, and whether they can retell what they've read. Reading levels and book selection: the 80% rule Research on reading development consistently points to one principle: kids grow as readers when they spend most of their time reading texts they can handle with moderate success [2]. Too easy and there's no growth. Too hard and they shut down. A practical framework: Independent reading (about 70% of reading time): books your child reads with 95%+ accuracy. These build fluency, stamina, and love of reading Instructional reading (about 20%): books at the edge of their ability (90-94% accuracy), read with support from a parent, teacher, or tutor. This is where growth happens Read-alouds and audiobooks (about 10%): books above their reading level but within their listening comprehension. These build vocabulary, background knowledge, and excitement about what's possible This is why a child's "level" should never become a ceiling. A fifth grader reading at a third grade Lexile level can still listen to and discuss The Lightning Thief (680L) as an audiobook. And a second grader reading at a fifth grade level still benefits from picture books that build inference and visual literacy skills. When to worry (and when not to) Reading level charts make it easy to spiral. If your kid is "behind," it feels urgent. If they're "ahead," you wonder if they're being challenged enough. A few things worth keeping in perspective: Below grade level doesn't always mean behind. Reading development has enormous natural variation, especially in kindergarten through second grade. Some kids don't click with reading until age 7 or 8 and then catch up rapidly. If your child is making consistent progress, even if it's slower than the chart suggests, that's often enough Persistent struggles deserve investigation. If your child is consistently reading two or more grade levels below peers by third grade, has difficulty with high-frequency words , or avoids reading despite plenty of access to books, it's worth exploring whether a learning difference like dyslexia might be involved. Our reading comprehension guide covers strategies, and teaching phonics at home can help with decoding gaps "Advanced" readers still need support. A child with a high Lexile score can decode complex text, but that doesn't mean they're emotionally ready for mature themes. Use the reading level to guide text complexity, but use your judgment as a parent to guide content Outschool reading classes by level If you're looking for reading support that meets your kid where they are, Outschool offers live, small-group reading classes and book clubs across every level, from emergent readers working on phonics to high schoolers analyzing literature. Teachers match instruction to your child's current ability, not a grade-level assumption. For kids who need targeted support, 1:1 reading tutoring lets a teacher assess your child's specific gaps and build a plan around them. Many families in ESA states use their funds to cover these classes through ClassWallet or Odyssey . Frequently asked questions What Lexile level should my kid be at? Lexile ranges by grade are guidelines, not benchmarks. A typical third grader falls between 520L and 820L, but many strong readers fall outside that range in either direction. Focus on whether your child is making progress and enjoying reading rather than hitting a specific number. How do I convert F&P levels to Lexile? There's no exact conversion because the systems measure different skills. The chart above shows approximate correlations. For example, F&P level M (late second to early third grade) roughly corresponds to Lexile 420L-650L. Use these as starting points for book selection, not as precise equivalents. Do homeschool families need to track reading levels? Not formally, unless your state requires standardized testing. Many homeschool families find that observing their child's reading habits, tracking books completed, and doing occasional informal assessments gives them enough information to guide instruction. That said, knowing your child's approximate Lexile range makes it easier to find books at the right challenge level. My child's Lexile score went down. Should I worry? Lexile scores can fluctuate between tests due to test conditions, the specific passages used, and normal variation in performance. A single dip is not cause for concern. If scores decline over two or more consecutive assessments, look at whether your child's reading volume has dropped or whether they might be struggling with a specific skill (fluency vs. comprehension vs. vocabulary). What reading level is Harry Potter? Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone has a Lexile of 880L, which falls in the fifth to sixth grade range. The later books in the series increase in complexity, with Order of the Phoenix at 950L and Deathly Hallows at 980L. Many fourth graders can read and enjoy the first book, especially if they're motivated by the story, even if the Lexile is technically above their assessed level. Sources [1] Fountas, I.C. & Pinnell, G.S. "Instructional Level Expectations for Reading." fountasandpinnell.com/resourcelibrary/resource?id=270 [2] Allington, R.L. "What Really Matters for Struggling Readers: Designing Research-Based Programs." 3rd ed., Pearson, 2012.

title: Apoyo Comunitario Después de un Sismo: Por Qué Importa | Blog Selia
summary: Cómo el apoyo comunitario y la solidaridad después de un sismo protegen la salud mental, reducen el aislamiento y ayudan a recuperar la estabilidad. Selia.
body_text: En Resumen Lo que encontrarás en este artículo: Por qué la comunidad protege la salud mental tras un desastre Cómo las redes de apoyo reducen el aislamiento y el estrés Formas concretas de sostener a tu comunidad después de un sismo Por qué cuidarte a ti también fortalece al grupo ¿Por qué la unión nos protege? Los seres humanos evolucionamos en grupo. Ante una amenaza, nuestro cerebro busca a los demás: la cercanía de otros es, biológicamente, una señal de seguridad. Por eso, después de un sismo, estar acompañado no es un lujo emocional, sino una necesidad que ayuda a regular el miedo. Cuando compartimos lo que vivimos con otros que también lo vivieron, algo se alivia. Descubrimos que nuestras reacciones son normales, que no estamos solos en el miedo, que hay personas dispuestas a sostenernos. Esa sensación de pertenencia amortigua el impacto emocional del desastre. Los psicólogos de Selia frecuentemente observan que las personas con redes de apoyo sólidas tienden a atravesar mejor las crisis. No porque sufran menos, sino porque no cargan solas con el peso. ¿Cómo el apoyo reduce el aislamiento? El aislamiento es uno de los grandes riesgos para la salud mental después de un desastre. Cuando alguien queda solo con su miedo, sin nadie con quien compartirlo, la angustia crece y la recuperación se hace más cuesta arriba. El silencio y la soledad alimentan el malestar. La comunidad rompe ese aislamiento. Una conversación, una comida compartida, saber que alguien pregunta cómo estás: gestos pequeños que le dicen a nuestro sistema nervioso "no estás en esto solo". Ese mensaje, repetido, ayuda a recuperar poco a poco la sensación de estabilidad. Las redes de apoyo también distribuyen la carga práctica. Cuando la comunidad se organiza para cubrir necesidades —comida, refugio, información, cuidado de niños y mayores—, cada persona siente menos que todo depende de ella. Y esa sensación de "podemos con esto juntos" es profundamente reparadora. ‍ Formas de sostener a tu comunidad No hace falta ser líder ni experto para aportar. La salud mental comunitaria se construye con gestos cotidianos al alcance de cualquiera. Puedes empezar por lo cercano: preguntar con sinceridad "¿cómo estás?" y quedarte a escuchar la respuesta. Revisar cómo están los vecinos que viven solos, los adultos mayores, las familias con niños pequeños. Compartir información confiable y frenar los rumores que aumentan el pánico. Y sumarte a las iniciativas de ayuda que surjan, según tus posibilidades. También ayuda cuidar el clima emocional colectivo: evitar difundir imágenes alarmantes sin necesidad, sostener espacios donde la gente pueda hablar de lo que siente sin juicio, y recordar juntos que el miedo que sienten es normal. A veces, la contribución más valiosa es simplemente estar presente. ¿Tu comunidad está atravesando el impacto de un sismo? Conoce cómo Selia acompaña a las personas afectadas → El cuidado también es colectivo Hay una idea que conviene recordar: para sostener a otros, también tienes que sostenerte a ti. Quien ayuda sin descanso, sin procesar su propio miedo, termina agotado y con menos para dar. Cuidarte no es egoísmo; es parte de cuidar al grupo. Date permiso de sentir, de pedir apoyo, de tomar pausas. Apóyate en otros cuando te toque a ti ser el que necesita. En una comunidad sana, el apoyo circula: hoy sostienes, mañana te sostienen. Esa reciprocidad es lo que mantiene fuerte al tejido colectivo. Si vives el impacto del sismo, cuidar tu propia salud mental es un buen punto de partida. Nuestra guía sobre qué hacer después de un sismo reúne acciones concretas para cuidarte a ti y a los tuyos. ¿Cuándo la comunidad no basta? El apoyo comunitario es poderoso, pero no reemplaza la ayuda profesional cuando hace falta. Hay personas que, pese a estar rodeadas de afecto, siguen atrapadas en el miedo, el insomnio o la angustia semanas después. En esos casos, el acompañamiento de un especialista marca la diferencia. Parte de cuidar a la comunidad es reconocer estas señales en los demás y animarlos, con cariño, a buscar apoyo profesional. Y también saber pedirlo para uno mismo. La comunidad y la terapia no compiten: se complementan. Preguntas Frecuentes ¿Por qué me siento mejor cuando hablo con otros que vivieron el sismo? Porque compartir la experiencia con quienes la vivieron valida lo que sientes y rompe el aislamiento. Descubres que tus reacciones son normales y que no estás solo. Esa sensación de pertenencia ayuda a regular el miedo. Es uno de los motivos por los que el apoyo comunitario protege tanto la salud mental tras un desastre. ¿Cómo puedo ayudar si yo también quedé afectado? Puedes ayudar desde tus posibilidades, sin exigirte de más. A veces el mejor aporte es cuidarte primero y luego ofrecer pequeños gestos: escuchar a un vecino, compartir información confiable, sumarte a una iniciativa cuando tengas energía. Ayudar puede ser reparador, pero no debe ser a costa de agotarte. El equilibrio también cuida a la comunidad. ¿La solidaridad después de un desastre realmente mejora la recuperación? La cercanía y el apoyo mutuo ayudan a las personas a sentirse más seguras y menos solas, lo que favorece la recuperación emocional. No elimina el dolor ni sustituye la ayuda profesional cuando se necesita, pero sí amortigua el impacto y fortalece la capacidad del grupo para salir adelante. Sentirse parte de un "nosotros" es profundamente protector. ¿Cómo cuido a los adultos mayores o personas vulnerables de mi comunidad? Mantén el contacto frecuente, revisa cómo están, ayúdalos con necesidades prácticas y escúchalos sin apurar. Muchas personas mayores prefieren no "molestar", así que acércate tú. Presta atención a señales de que alguien está muy afectado o aislado, y ayúdalo a conectar con apoyo, incluida ayuda profesional si hace falta. Conclusión Después de un sismo, la unión no es solo un acto de solidaridad: es una forma real de cuidar la salud mental de todos. Las redes de apoyo reducen el aislamiento, distribuyen la carga y le recuerdan a cada persona que no está sola en el miedo. Cada gesto cuenta: una escucha, una comida compartida, un "aquí estoy". Y cuando la comunidad no alcanza, buscar ayuda profesional es otra forma de cuidarse juntos. Porque salimos adelante mejor cuando lo hacemos acompañados. Nota importante : Este artículo tiene fines informativos y no reemplaza el consejo de un profesional de salud mental. Si tú o alguien de tu comunidad presenta señales de malestar que se prolongan o afectan la vida diaria, te recomendamos consultar con un especialista. En situaciones de crisis, busca ayuda inmediata: en Colombia, Línea 106; en México, SAPTEL 55 5259-8121; en España, Teléfono de la Esperanza 717 003 717.

title: Pennsylvania American Water Announces Service Line Identification Outreach
summary: Door-to-door outreach in the Pittston area advances lead service line replacement program and helps customers access replacement opportunities at no direct cost SCRANTON, Pa. (August 4, 2026) –...
body_text: Door-to-door outreach in the Pittston area advances lead service line replacement program and helps customers access replacement opportunities at no direct cost SCRANTON, Pa. (August 4, 2026) – Pennsylvania American Water today announced door-to-door canvassing outreach in the Pittston area to assist nearly 2,000 customers in identifying the material of their home’s water service line. “Customer involvement makes this work possible,” said Pennsylvania American Water Vice President of Operations Jim Runzer. “Our goal is to catalog the material type of customers’ service lines to help safeguard the quality of water for our customers.” A water service line is a pipe that connects a home or business to the water main in the street. Pennsylvania American Water owns a portion of the service line, typically from the main to the curb stop, found near the street curb or sidewalk. The property owner owns the rest of the service line (from curb stop) all the way into the house or building being served, which is why customer participation in this program is important. If a service line is identified as lead or galvanized steel, Pennsylvania American Water will work with the customer to replace the line at no direct cost to them. In Pittston, approximately 1,950 customer-side water service line materials have not yet been identified, and in Lackawanna and Luzerne counties, the material of approximately 76,400 service lines have not been identified. Outreach is also currently underway in Scranton and Carbondale. Once complete, efforts will continue in other communities served by the company’s system in Lackawanna and Luzerne counties. The door‑to‑door outreach will be conducted by CDM Smith, Pennsylvania American Water’s service line Inventory contractor. All representatives will carry official company photo I.D. badges and wear logoed, high-visibility vests. Canvassing in the area is expected to be completed in these areas in the fall. The outreach efforts are part of the company’s lead service line replacement program, supporting the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Lead and Copper Rule Improvements, which require all water utilities to identify and make public the materials that both company-owned and customer-owned service lines are made of to address and minimize exposure of lead in drinking water. Since the lead service line identification project began, more than 50,000 service lines have been identified statewide, and more than 3,400 customer-owned lead lines have been replaced. Customers can view an interactive service line map at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/LeadFacts , self‑report their service line material online, or request assistance by calling 717‑581‑8599, emailing LeadFreePA@amwater.com or scheduling an appointment at calendly.com/LeadFreePA . About American Water American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. body_text: Skin dysmorphia can turn normal skin concerns into overwhelming anxiety. Learn the signs, causes, social media impact, and ways to seek support. The desire for healthy, clear skin is common. Many people invest time and money into skincare routines, treatments, and products because they want to feel confident in their appearance. However, for some individuals, concerns about their skin can become overwhelming and begin to affect their mental health, relationships, finances, and everyday life. Skin dysmorphia, sometimes linked with acne dysmorphia, is a form of body dysmorphic disorder (BDD). It involves an intense focus on perceived flaws in the skin that may be minor or not visible to others. A person experiencing this condition may believe their skin looks severely damaged, even when friends, family members, or professionals do not see the same issue. For those affected, the problem is not simply wanting better skin. It becomes a constant cycle of checking, comparing, worrying, and trying to “fix” something they believe is wrong. What Does Skin Dysmorphia Feel Like? People with skin dysmorphia often describe spending hours thinking about their appearance. Looking in the mirror can become a stressful experience rather than a normal part of daily life. Some common thoughts include: Believing other people are staring at skin imperfections Feeling embarrassed or ashamed about appearance Avoiding social events because of skin concerns Constantly checking mirrors, photos, or phone cameras Comparing skin to influencers or celebrities online Feeling unable to focus on conversations because of worries about appearance Over time, these thoughts can become exhausting. Some people may withdraw from friends, avoid certain lighting, cover their face with makeup, or stop participating in activities they previously enjoyed. The Connection Between Social Media and Skin Anxiety The rise of skincare content online has created both positive and negative effects. Educational videos can help people understand ingredients, routines, and professional advice. However, social media platforms also frequently show edited images, filters, carefully controlled lighting, and unrealistic beauty standards. Platforms such as TikTok and Instagram often present flawless-looking skin as normal. Many images are enhanced through editing, makeup, camera settings, or professional treatments. When users compare their real skin with carefully created online content, they may develop unrealistic expectations. Research into appearance concerns has suggested that increased exposure to idealised beauty content can contribute to higher levels of dissatisfaction and anxiety for some users. The skincare industry has also expanded rapidly, with thousands of products marketed as solutions for every possible concern. This can encourage the belief that perfect skin is achievable if the right product, routine, or treatment is found. When Skincare Becomes Excessive A healthy skincare routine can support skin health, but excessive routines may create problems. Some people experiencing skin dysmorphia may repeatedly purchase new products, undergo unnecessary treatments, or use harsh ingredients in an attempt to improve their appearance. Overuse of active skincare ingredients, aggressive exfoliation, or constant product changes can irritate the skin and potentially lead to redness, sensitivity, dryness, or damage. Experts warn that some people become trapped in a cycle where every small breakout or change in their skin creates panic. Instead of seeing normal skin changes as temporary, they may interpret them as proof that something is seriously wrong. The Emotional and Financial Impact Skin dysmorphia can affect much more than appearance. Many people report experiencing anxiety, low confidence, depression, and isolation. Some individuals spend large amounts of money on skincare products, cosmetic procedures, or treatments while searching for a solution. However, because the underlying concern is connected to perception and mental health, external treatments may not provide lasting relief. A person may achieve clearer skin but still feel dissatisfied because the distress comes from how they view themselves rather than the actual condition of their skin. Why Professional Support Matters Because skin dysmorphia involves appearance concerns, many people first seek help from dermatologists or aesthetic professionals. While treating genuine skin conditions is important, some individuals may also need psychological support. Mental health professionals can help people understand appearance-related thoughts and develop healthier ways of responding to them. Treatment approaches for body dysmorphic disorder may include therapies such as cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), which can help people recognise harmful thought patterns and reduce compulsive behaviours. Healthcare professionals are increasingly recognising the importance of collaboration between dermatologists, aesthetic practitioners, and mental health specialists. How to Recognise Possible Warning Signs It may be helpful to consider whether skin concerns are affecting your quality of life. Possible warning signs include: Spending large amounts of time thinking about skin Frequently checking mirrors or photographs Buying many skincare products without feeling satisfied Avoiding social situations because of appearance worries Feeling that your self-worth depends on having perfect skin Experiencing intense distress over minor imperfections A useful question to ask is: “Is my skincare routine helping me feel confident, or is it controlling my life?” Building a Healthier Relationship With Your Skin Healthy skin does not mean flawless skin. Everyone experiences pores, texture, blemishes, ageing, and changes over time. These are normal parts of having human skin. Creating a balanced approach may involve: Following a simple routine recommended by qualified professionals Limiting comparisons with edited online images Taking breaks from appearance-focused social media content Focusing on overall wellbeing rather than perfection Seeking support if worries become overwhelming Skin health is connected to sleep, nutrition, stress levels, hormones, and general health. Looking after yourself involves more than chasing an ideal appearance. Final Thoughts The desire for better skin is normal, but constant fear and dissatisfaction can become harmful. Skin dysmorphia shows how beauty pressures and mental health can become closely connected. Recognising the signs early can help people seek appropriate support and move away from exhausting cycles of comparison and self-criticism. Healthy skin does not require perfection, and confidence should not depend on meeting unrealistic beauty standards. Sources The Independent, August 04, 2026. Disclaimer This article is for informational purposes only and is not medical advice. If you are experiencing severe distress, anxiety, depression, or obsessive thoughts about your appearance, consider speaking with a qualified healthcare professional or mental health specialist. In the UK and Republic of Ireland, confidential emotional support is available through Samaritans by calling 116 123.
